description:
## Goal

Restore the fz_f98_range_map_converges run-path compiler and execution work budget after the RuntimeDemand cutover before changing any fixture timeout policy.

## CI evidence

Under the same GitHub cargo llvm-cov job, the elapsed interval ending at matrix::fz_f98_range_map_converges::run was approximately:
- main a3a9761d1: 1.47s, pass
- fz-kdt.47 b533b965: 3.02s, timeout
- fz-tfn.3 8859a37f: 2.95s, pass just under the limit
- fz-kdt.72 c7235335: 3.02s, timeout
- fz-tfn.17 548dbd87: 3.02s, timeout
- fz-kdt.45 446374021: 2.25s, pass

The first epic commit therefore introduced a material regression; later direct ExecutableFacts work recovers only part of it. The three-second gate is currently detecting real movement and must not be raised first.

## Strategy and TDD

1. Reproduce main versus each epic commit with identical instrumentation and repeated clean runs.
2. Compare deterministic scheduler evaluations, product settlements/evaluations/cache behavior, RuntimeDemand work, semantic facts, backend/native body and byte counts, and runtime output.
3. Identify the first additional work introduced by fz-kdt.47 and trace it to exact formula/dependency ownership.
4. Add a work-budget regression that fails on the current epic head and passes only when the extra work is removed.
5. Remove or fold the redundant work at its authoritative data-model boundary; do not special-case this fixture or relax a time limit.
6. Prove outputs/artifacts and determinism unchanged, and run target three doors, full library, serial matrix, fz2_cli, strict clippy and formatting.

## Acceptance

Current epic head returns to mainline-or-better deterministic work counts and a comparable instrumented run distribution. Any remaining wall-clock variance must be explained by equal-or-lower work before fz-kdt.175 may reconsider the hang guard.
title: Restore range-map work budget after RuntimeDemand cutover
